name: ACME Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (CLD Flame)

objective.value: Provide the benchmark experimental data needed to rigorously test computational models at the extremes of the fuel-dilution spectrum: (A) characterize weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene versus velocity and fuel dilution via flame shape, lift-off height, temperature and extinction limits; (B) characterize the sooting tendencies of diffusion flames with long residence times via flame shape, gas temperature in the soot-free region, soot luminosity, soot temperature and soot volume fraction.

fuel_geometry.value: Axisymmetric (coaxial) coflow burner: gaseous fuel (or a fuel/nitrogen mixture) issues from a central small tube into an annular air coflow, with a gas-permeable (honeycomb) outlet across the annulus about 3 mm below the inner-tube tip. The inner fuel tube has a 2.1 mm inside diameter and a 2.4 mm outside diameter. Lifted (detached) flames are the focus so flame behaviour does not depend on heat loss to the burner.

sources.note: ACME overview: lifted flames are used as the basis for the research to avoid flame dependence on heat loss to the burner; measurements of methane and ethylene flames in an air coflow

ACME Integrated Science Requirements Document (ISRD), section 1.4 Coflow Burner (CLD Flame): small inner tube (2.1 mm ID, 2.4 mm OD) inside a larger outer tube, coflow gas (e.g., air) through the annulus; honeycomb outlet ~3 mm below the inner-tube tip

ACME overview: measurements of the structure of diluted methane and ethylene flames in an air coflow; the oxidizer stream is air, i.e. about 21% O2 by volume balanced with nitrogen

o2_percent.note: Inferred: oxidizer is air coflow (~21% O2); not a swept variable; PSI experimental table has no atmospheric-oxygen column.

pressure_psi.note: No CLD-Flame-specific tested pressure was found. The PSI experimental table (tables/PSI-21.csv) has no pressure column and the ACME overview does not state one. The ACME ISRD requires an initial CIR chamber pressure of 0.1-3 bar absolute (about 1.45-43.5 psi) for ACME tests, but that is a hardware/design requirement, not measured test data, so it is not recorded here.

sources.note: ACME ISRD, coflow burner requirements: burner flow profile measured/verified for velocities up to 50 cm/s, with matched inner/annulus velocities in 10 cm/s increments from 20 to 50 cm/s and an explicit 10 cm/s matched case; unmatched pairs span 0 to 50 cm/s
ACME summary slides (CSSCI 2022): CH* profiles reported as a function of matched fuel and coflow velocities at 10, 20, 30 and 40 cm/s

airflow.note: Inferred from hardware requirements (ISRD) and summary slides showing 10-40 cm/s matched velocities actually used; PSI experimental table reports only burner gas flows in slpm, not coflow velocity.

relevance_notes.value: CLD Flame is fundamental laminar non-premixed-flame research whose secondary purpose (per the ACME project) is spacecraft fire prevention. Its microgravity soot and dilution/extinction-limit measurements provide benchmark data for flammability and flame-stability models that the brief says underpin material selection and fire safety. The brief names ACME only among investigations that are relevant to fire safety 'just not as strongly or directly', so treat it as supporting evidence rather than a direct prevention study.
